rules.rule: Serial number missing on hardware classes
rules.what_it_means: Hardware-class CIs have no serial number. Serial is an identity attribute used by the identification engine.
rules.why_it_matters: Not a cosmetic gap. IRE uses serial to recognise a device it has seen before; without it, every rediscovery is a candidate for a new record. This rule is a direct cause of Group 4 duplicates.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci_hardware and subclasses, serial_number field
rules.detection_logic: Hardware-class CIs WHERE serial_number is empty OR matches placeholder pattern
rules.threshold_parameter: Placeholder set: unknown, n/a, tbd, none, -, null, 0, default, to be filled
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on emptiness. Placeholder detection confidence 95% (regex may catch a legitimate value).
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list by class with the serial field state, plus the identification rule that consumes serial for that class.
rules.false_positive_guard: Virtual CIs and cloud instances legitimately have no serial. Scope this rule to physical hardware classes only.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 — source serial from discovery or asset, then bulk apply
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes CMDB-035, CMDB-041; caused by ITOM discovery failure

rules.rule: FQDN / IP / MAC missing on network-addressable classes
rules.what_it_means: Network-addressable CIs have no FQDN, IP address or MAC address populated.
rules.why_it_matters: These are the fields event binding and discovery matching rely on. Missing them means alerts cannot resolve to this CI and discovery cannot reconcile it. This is the shape that produced the router demo failure.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci with network-addressable class flag; fqdn, ip_address, mac_address fields
rules.detection_logic: Network-addressable classes WHERE all three of fqdn, ip_address, mac_address are empty or placeholder
rules.threshold_parameter: Class set configurable. Default: all classes under cmdb_ci_netgear, cmdb_ci_computer, cmdb_ci_appl
rules.confidence_basis: 100% where all three empty. 80% where one populated and two empty (may be legitimate for the class).
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list, the three field states, the em_match_rule that would consume them, and recent alert binding attempts against these CIs.
rules.false_positive_guard: Logical CIs, business applications and non-addressable classes. Restrict class scope tightly.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 1
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes ITOM event binding failure; caused by discovery credential failure

rules.rule: Identity attributes missing on classes with an identification rule that uses them
rules.what_it_means: Identity attributes are missing specifically on classes whose identification rule consumes them — serial on a class identified by serial, IP on a class identified by IP.
rules.why_it_matters: This is the precise intersection that produces duplicates. A missing serial on a class that does not use serial for identification is a completeness gap; on a class that does, it is a guarantee that the next discovery run creates a second record.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_identifier_entry criterion attributes per class, CI attribute population for exactly those attributes
rules.detection_logic: For each class: the attribute set its identification rule consumes; count CIs where any of those attributes is empty or placeholder
rules.threshold_parameter: Derived per class from the identification rule, not a fixed attribute list
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the join between rule criteria and attribute state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Class, its identification criteria, the CI count missing each criterion attribute, and the duplicate count already present in that class.
rules.false_positive_guard: Classes with multiple identification entries where an alternative criterion is populated. Flag only where all criteria are unmet.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 — source the attribute, then bulk apply
rules.cross_domain_link: The precise predictor of future duplicates; joins CMDB-044 and CMDB-033

rules.rule: Business criticality unpopulated on impact-feeding classes
rules.what_it_means: Business criticality is unpopulated on classes that feed impact calculation.
rules.why_it_matters: Impact analysis can identify affected CIs but cannot rank them. Every affected service looks equally important, so prioritisation during an incident is guesswork.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.business_criticality on classes referenced by impact rules
rules.detection_logic: CIs in impact-feeding classes WHERE business_criticality is empty
rules.threshold_parameter: Class set = classes participating in service maps or impact rules
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on emptiness. Recommendation confidence derives from inferring criticality from parent service.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list, the services they support, and the criticality of those services where known.
rules.false_positive_guard: Non-production CIs where criticality is intentionally unset.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where inferable from parent service, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Degrades ITSM prioritisation and Event Management impact ranking

rules.rule: Environment / used\_for unpopulated
rules.what_it_means: The environment field (used_for) is empty, so production and non-production CIs are indistinguishable.
rules.why_it_matters: Change risk assessment, SLA applicability and impact calculation all treat these CIs identically to production. A non-production CI can trigger a production-grade response, and vice versa.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.used_for, application service used_for
rules.detection_logic: CIs in classes where used_for is defined WHERE value is empty
rules.threshold_parameter: Class scope configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on emptiness. Inference confidence from naming convention, parent service, and discovery range.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list with any inferable environment signal: name pattern, IP range, parent service environment.
rules.false_positive_guard: Classes where environment is not a meaningful concept.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where strongly inferable, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Affects Change risk, SLA applicability, ITSM routing

rules.rule: Placeholder value in a required attribute
rules.what_it_means: A required attribute contains a placeholder value rather than real data: unknown, n/a, TBD, -, null-as-string, 0.0.0.0.
rules.why_it_matters: The field reads as populated to every completeness metric, so the reported completeness is inflated. This rule typically drops a customer's self-reported completeness by 10-20 points, which is the moment they start trusting your numbers over their dashboard.
rules.source_tables_fields: All required attributes across principal classes
rules.detection_logic: Required attributes matching the placeholder pattern set, case-insensitive, trimmed
rules.threshold_parameter: Placeholder set configurable per estate. Default 12 patterns including 0.0.0.0 and 00:00:00:00:00:00.
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — regex could theoretically match a legitimate value. Review the top 20 matches per pattern before bulk action.
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by attribute and by pattern, with sample records. Show reported completeness vs placeholder-adjusted completeness side by side.
rules.false_positive_guard: A legitimate value that resembles a placeholder. Always show samples before applying.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — the correct value must be sourced, not guessed
rules.cross_domain_link: Inflates D1; reveals the gap between reported and actual completeness

rules.rule: Mandatory class attributes missing
rules.what_it_means: CIs in principal classes are missing attributes their class declares mandatory.
rules.why_it_matters: Standard completeness. Its value is in weighting: missing attributes on principal classes carry operational consequence, unlike the same gap on peripheral classes.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_dictionary mandatory flags per class, cmdb_health_inclusion_rule required attribute config, CI records
rules.detection_logic: Per principal class: CIs where any mandatory attribute is empty or placeholder
rules.threshold_parameter: Per-class attribute list from config. Identity attributes weighted 3x.
rules.confidence_basis: Computed as populated required attributes / total required attributes per CI.
rules.evidence_to_show: Per-class completeness heatmap, drill to CI list, drill to specific empty attribute.
rules.false_positive_guard: Attribute mandatory in dictionary but genuinely not applicable to a subclass. Maintain per-class exclusions.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 where source data exists

rules.rule: Company unpopulated on multi-company instances
rules.what_it_means: On a multi-company instance, CIs have no company populated.
rules.why_it_matters: Domain separation, cost allocation and cross-entity reporting all break. In a group structure this is a regulatory reporting gap, not just a data gap.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.company, core_company count, sys_domain if active
rules.detection_logic: IF core_company count > 1: CIs WHERE company is empty
rules.threshold_parameter: Only fires when more than one active company exists
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on emptiness, conditional on multi-company detection.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI count by class, plus the company list and which companies have zero CIs assigned.
rules.false_positive_guard: Single-company instance with legacy company records. Check for active company count, not total.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where inferable from location or support group, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Affects domain separation and financial reporting

rules.rule: Location missing or pointing to a catch-all
rules.what_it_means: Location is empty, or points to a generic catch-all location such as 'India' or 'Head Office' that carries no operational meaning.
rules.why_it_matters: Incident routing, DR scoping, asset reconciliation and location-based impact rules all degrade. The catch-all case is worse than empty because it reads as populated.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.location, cmn_location hierarchy depth
rules.detection_logic: CIs WHERE location empty OR location resolves to a node above the configured minimum hierarchy depth
rules.threshold_parameter: Minimum depth default 3 (country > city > site). Configurable.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on emptiness. 85% on catch-all detection, since depth is a proxy for specificity.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI count by location, ranked. Show the catch-all locations with disproportionate CI counts.
rules.false_positive_guard: Cloud resources with no physical location. Scope out cloud classes.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where inferable from discovery schedule location, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Caused by ITOM-004 (location not defined on discovery schedule)

rules.rule: Recommended attributes missing
rules.what_it_means: CIs are missing attributes configured as recommended rather than mandatory for their class.
rules.why_it_matters: Lower consequence than mandatory gaps but material in aggregate. Recommended attributes are typically what makes a CI useful rather than merely valid.
rules.source_tables_fields: Recommended attribute config per class, CI records
rules.detection_logic: Per principal class: CIs where any recommended attribute is empty or placeholder
rules.threshold_parameter: Per-class list from health config
rules.confidence_basis: Computed as populated / total recommended per CI.
rules.evidence_to_show: Per-class heatmap with drill to attribute.
rules.false_positive_guard: Recommended attribute not applicable to a subclass.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where sourceable, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Attribute at unchanged default choice value
rules.what_it_means: An attribute holds the class default choice value and has never been changed since CI creation.
rules.why_it_matters: Suggests the field was never considered rather than deliberately set. Weak signal alone, strong in aggregate across a class.
rules.source_tables_fields: CI attribute values, sys_choice defaults, sys_audit for change history
rules.detection_logic: CIs where attribute = class default AND no audit entry for that field
rules.threshold_parameter: Applies to choice fields only
rules.confidence_basis: 70% — the default may be correct for many CIs. Report as a class-level pattern, not per record.
rules.evidence_to_show: Percentage of CIs in the class at default, with the distribution of non-default values for contrast.
rules.false_positive_guard: Default genuinely correct for most CIs in the class. Present as a ratio, never as individual findings.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Financial attributes missing
rules.what_it_means: Cost centre and financial attributes are unpopulated.
rules.why_it_matters: Low operational consequence, real financial consequence. Blocks showback, chargeback and TCO reporting.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.cost_center, asset financial fields
rules.detection_logic: CIs in classes with financial relevance WHERE cost_center empty
rules.threshold_parameter: Class scope configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on emptiness.
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by class and by owning group, with the cost centres that do have CIs for contrast.
rules.false_positive_guard: Organisation does not do CI-level cost allocation. Confirm before raising.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where inferable from department or owner, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Attribute contradicted by its authoritative source
rules.what_it_means: An attribute value is contradicted by the source that holds precedence for it. Discovery says one thing, the CMDB holds another.
rules.why_it_matters: This is a wrong answer, not a missing one, which is materially worse. Systems act on it. The reconciliation precedence exists precisely to prevent this and is not being honoured.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_metadata / last-seen data per attribute, reconciliation precedence config, discovery payloads
rules.detection_logic: For attributes with a defined precedence source: flag where the CMDB value differs from the most recent value reported by that source
rules.threshold_parameter: Tolerance window for legitimate lag, default 24h
rules.confidence_basis: Computed from source recency and count of corroborating sources. Higher where two sources agree against the CMDB.
rules.evidence_to_show: Attribute, CMDB value, source value, source, timestamp, and precedence configuration.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate manual override with documented justification. Check for an override flag or annotation.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — apply the precedence source value, snapshot held

rules.rule: install\_status and operational\_status contradictory
rules.what_it_means: install_status and operational_status hold a combination the platform does not consider valid: for example Retired and Operational, or Absent and Running.
rules.why_it_matters: Every consumer reads one field or the other and gets a different answer. Reports disagree, impact rules misfire, and nobody can say whether the CI is live.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.install_status, cmdb_ci.operational_status, permitted combination set
rules.detection_logic: CIs where the (install_status, operational_status) pair is not in the permitted set
rules.threshold_parameter: Permitted set read from the instance configuration, not hardcoded
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — combination is in the permitted set or it is not.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list grouped by invalid combination, with counts, plus corroborating signals: last_discovered, open tasks, relationship state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Customer has extended the choice lists and the permitted set is not documented. Read the instance's own set.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where corroborating evidence resolves it, Lane 3 where contradictory

rules.rule: Reclassification churn between discovery runs
rules.what_it_means: A CI changes sys_class_name repeatedly across discovery runs, flipping between two or more classes.
rules.why_it_matters: Each reclassification can drop class-specific attributes and relationships. The CI never stabilises, so nothing built on it is reliable. Usually indicates competing patterns or competing sources.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_audit on sys_class_name, discovery_device_history
rules.detection_logic: CIs with more than N sys_class_name changes in the observation window
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 3 changes in 90 days. Configurable.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on detection from audit history. Root cause attribution 85%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Class change timeline per CI, the sources or patterns responsible for each change, and the attributes lost at each transition.
rules.false_positive_guard: A genuine one-time reclassification project. Look for a cluster in a single window rather than ongoing churn.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — pattern or precedence correction
rules.cross_domain_link: Caused by ITOM pattern conflict or duplicate source; causes attribute loss

rules.rule: CI in the wrong class for its attributes
rules.what_it_means: A CI's attributes indicate it belongs in a different class than the one it sits in: a record with a serial number and management IP sitting in a logical or application class.
rules.why_it_matters: Class-appropriate rules never apply. Identification, relationship validation and attribute requirements are all wrong for this record.
rules.source_tables_fields: CI attributes vs class attribute profile derived from the estate
rules.detection_logic: CIs whose populated attribute signature better matches another class profile by a margin
rules.threshold_parameter: Margin threshold configurable. Default: target class match 2x current class match.
rules.confidence_basis: Computed from attribute signature overlap. Report the margin.
rules.evidence_to_show: The CI, its attributes, its current class profile match, and the better-matching class with its profile.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely hybrid entities. Require a clear margin before flagging.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: CI sitting on base cmdb\_ci
rules.what_it_means: CIs sit on the base cmdb_ci class rather than a specific subclass.
rules.why_it_matters: Class-specific attributes, identification rules and relationship rules do not apply. The CI is effectively untyped and cannot be governed by any class-scoped rule.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci WHERE sys_class_name = 'cmdb_ci'
rules.detection_logic: COUNT and list of CIs on the base class
rules.threshold_parameter: Any count above zero
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on detection. Reclassification recommendation confidence derives from available attributes.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list with populated attributes, and the class SAOS would infer from those attributes.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate use of base class for a non-standard entity. Rare; question it.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 — reclassification is consequential
rules.cross_domain_link: Excluded from most class-scoped rules, so inflates other scores

rules.rule: Value outside the permitted choice list
rules.what_it_means: An attribute holds a value that is not present in the sys_choice list for that field.
rules.why_it_matters: Usually arrives via import or API bypassing UI validation. Breaks reporting grouping and any logic that switches on the choice value.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_choice per field, CI attribute values
rules.detection_logic: For choice fields: values not present in the active sys_choice set for that table and element
rules.threshold_parameter: Include inherited choices from parent tables
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — value is in the list or it is not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Value, count, the valid choice list, and the source that wrote the value where determinable.
rules.false_positive_guard: Choice recently retired while records still hold the old value legitimately. Check sys_choice inactive entries.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where mapping to a valid value is unambiguous, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Indicates an import or integration bypassing validation

rules.rule: Format validation failure (IP, MAC, serial, FQDN)
rules.what_it_means: An attribute value fails format validation for its type: malformed IP, invalid MAC, serial not matching the manufacturer pattern, FQDN without a domain.
rules.why_it_matters: Matching and identification silently fail on malformed values. The field looks populated and is unusable.
rules.source_tables_fields: IP, MAC, FQDN, serial fields across relevant classes
rules.detection_logic: Regex validation per field type; flag non-conforming populated values
rules.threshold_parameter: Pattern set per field type, extensible per manufacturer for serial
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — some legitimate values fail naive patterns, particularly serials.
rules.evidence_to_show: Value, expected pattern, count by class, and sample records.
rules.false_positive_guard: Manufacturer-specific serial formats not in the pattern set. Build the pattern library from the estate's own dominant formats.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — correction requires the real value
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes identification and event binding failure

rules.rule: Impossible numeric values
rules.what_it_means: Numeric attributes hold impossible values: zero RAM, negative disk, CPU count of zero, capacity larger than physically possible.
rules.why_it_matters: Indicates a failed discovery parse or a bad transform. The CI carries data that is confidently wrong.
rules.source_tables_fields: Numeric CI attributes: ram, disk_space, cpu_count, capacity
rules.detection_logic: Values outside configured plausible ranges per attribute
rules.threshold_parameter: Ranges configurable per attribute and class
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on range violation. Cause attribution from source.
rules.evidence_to_show: Value, plausible range, count, source, and the discovery or transform that wrote it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately zero for virtual or logical CIs. Scope by class.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — clear to null and let discovery repopulate, or Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Indicates ITOM sensor or transform failure

rules.rule: Name violating the estate's own dominant convention
rules.what_it_means: CI names do not conform to the estate's own dominant naming convention, derived from the majority pattern rather than an imposed standard.
rules.why_it_matters: Low consequence. Matters for fuzzy duplicate detection and human searchability. Deliberately Low severity.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.name by class, pattern frequency analysis
rules.detection_logic: Derive dominant name pattern per class from frequency; flag names below similarity threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Dominant pattern must cover at least 60% of the class before the rule fires
rules.confidence_basis: 70% — convention inference is probabilistic. Report as a ratio.
rules.evidence_to_show: Dominant pattern, conformance percentage, and non-conforming samples.
rules.false_positive_guard: Estate has multiple legitimate conventions by region or source. Suppress where no single pattern reaches 60%.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Asymmetric duplicate — one with relationships, one without
rules.what_it_means: Two or more CIs describe the same physical thing, and one carries relationships while the other has none.
rules.why_it_matters: The most dangerous record state in a CMDB. Monitoring and events bind to the empty twin, impact analysis traverses from it, and returns a confident zero. This is exactly what produced the router outage: the alert was correct, the CI was correct, the answer was empty.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci identity attributes, cmdb_rel_ci edge counts per CI
rules.detection_logic: Duplicate sets (by serial, IP, MAC, FQDN or correlation_id) where at least one member has zero edges and at least one has edges
rules.threshold_parameter: Any asymmetric set. Weight 5x a symmetric duplicate in scoring.
rules.confidence_basis: Computed from identity attribute match strength: exact serial match 97%, IP+name 92%, fuzzy name+IP 85%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both CI records side by side, their identity attributes, edge counts, creation source and date, and any alert or task bound to each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate logical-plus-physical modelling (a cluster CI and its members). Check class pair against the modelling convention.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — designate survivor, re-point references, retire the other, transfer correlation_id
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes ITOM event binding failure; caused by CMDB-044/045/047

rules.rule: Serial number duplicate
rules.what_it_means: The same serial number appears on more than one CI.
rules.why_it_matters: Serial is a strong identity attribute. A duplicate serial means either two records for one device, or a discovery source writing a shared or default serial across many devices.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.serial_number across all classes
rules.detection_logic: Serial values appearing on more than one active CI, excluding placeholder values
rules.threshold_parameter: Exclude placeholders and serials appearing on more than N CIs (likely a default value, not a duplicate)
rules.confidence_basis: 97% on exact match of a valid serial. Drops sharply if the serial appears on many CIs.
rules.evidence_to_show: All CIs sharing the serial, their classes, sources, creation dates and edge counts.
rules.false_positive_guard: A manufacturer default serial written across a device family. Detect by frequency: a serial on 400 CIs is a bad default, not 400 duplicates.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 for true pairs, Lane 2 to fix the source writing bad defaults

rules.rule: FQDN / IP / MAC duplicate
rules.what_it_means: The same FQDN, IP address or MAC address appears on more than one CI.
rules.why_it_matters: Network identity collision. Discovery and event binding cannot resolve which record is correct.
rules.source_tables_fields: fqdn, ip_address, mac_address across classes
rules.detection_logic: Address values on more than one active CI, excluding documented shared-address cases
rules.threshold_parameter: Exclude loopback, link-local, 0.0.0.0, and configured VIP ranges
rules.confidence_basis: IP match 88% (addresses are reassigned), MAC match 95%, FQDN match 93%.
rules.evidence_to_show: All CIs sharing the address, with last_discovered, source, and class.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate shared addresses: VIPs, clusters, load balancers, NAT. Maintain an exclusion range list.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 for true duplicates, Lane 3 for cluster modelling
rules.cross_domain_link: Direct cause of discovery and event binding ambiguity

rules.rule: correlation\_id duplicate
rules.what_it_means: The same correlation_id appears on more than one CI.
rules.why_it_matters: correlation_id is the external system's key. A duplicate means two CMDB records claim to be the same external object, and the integration will write to whichever it finds first.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.correlation_id
rules.detection_logic: correlation_id values on more than one active CI
rules.threshold_parameter: Exclude empty and placeholder
rules.confidence_basis: 98% — correlation_id is an explicit external key, so a collision is almost always a real duplicate.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both CIs, the external source, and the integration that writes the correlation_id.
rules.false_positive_guard: Two external systems legitimately using the same key space. Check source field.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1

rules.rule: Name duplicate across classes
rules.what_it_means: The same name exists on CIs in two different classes.
rules.why_it_matters: Name-based matching, which most event connectors and many integrations use, cannot disambiguate. Binding becomes arbitrary.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.name across classes
rules.detection_logic: Names appearing in more than one class, excluding intentional class-pair conventions
rules.threshold_parameter: Case-insensitive, trimmed, with configurable normalisation (strip domain suffix)
rules.confidence_basis: Match confidence 90% on exact normalised name, lower where names are generic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both records, their classes, identity attributes, and the match rules that would consume the name.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate parent-child modelling across classes with the same name. Maintain a permitted class-pair list.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 or Lane 3 depending on which is the real record

rules.rule: Duplicate rate trending up
rules.what_it_means: The rate at which new duplicates are created is rising over time.
rules.why_it_matters: Tells you the factory is broken, not just the output. Remediating duplicates while the creation rate rises is bailing a boat without patching the hull. This is the finding that justifies fixing identification rules first.
rules.source_tables_fields: Duplicate set membership over successive assessment snapshots
rules.detection_logic: New duplicate sets per week, trended across the observation window
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires at least 3 snapshots. Flag on positive trend above noise threshold.
rules.confidence_basis: Trend confidence from sample count and variance. State the window explicitly.
rules.evidence_to_show: Trend chart, new duplicates per week, and attribution by creating source.
rules.false_positive_guard: A one-time integration onboarding creating a burst. Look for sustained trend, not a spike.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — fix the identification rules and the source

rules.rule: Duplicates from two different discovery sources
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate CIs were created by two different discovery or integration sources that IRE failed to merge.
rules.why_it_matters: Names the specific source pair responsible, which turns a pile of duplicates into a fixable integration problem.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.discovery_source on duplicate set members
rules.detection_logic: Duplicate sets whose members have differing discovery_source values, grouped by source pair
rules.threshold_parameter: Report by source pair, ranked by count
rules.confidence_basis: Inherits the duplicate detection confidence; source attribution is 100%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Duplicate count by source pair, with sample sets and the identification rule that should have matched them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Sources legitimately creating different CI types that happen to share an attribute.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — identification rule and source precedence correction
rules.cross_domain_link: Points directly at the responsible ITOM or integration config

rules.rule: Exact name duplicate within class
rules.what_it_means: The same name appears on more than one CI within the same class.
rules.why_it_matters: The most basic duplicate shape and the easiest to remediate. Lower severity than cross-class because class context at least narrows the ambiguity.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.name grouped by sys_class_name
rules.detection_logic: Names on more than one active CI within a class, normalised
rules.threshold_parameter: Normalisation configurable: case, whitespace, domain suffix
rules.confidence_basis: 90% on exact normalised match within class.
rules.evidence_to_show: All CIs sharing the name, with identity attributes, sources, and edge counts.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately identical names on genuinely different devices (rare but occurs with generic names like 'localhost').
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1

rules.rule: Fuzzy near-duplicate with matching identity attribute
rules.what_it_means: CI names are near-matches rather than exact, but an identity attribute (serial, IP, MAC) matches exactly.
rules.why_it_matters: Catches the duplicates that exact-match rules miss: hostname vs FQDN, different casing, trailing domain, abbreviations. Usually the largest single duplicate population in an estate.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.name with fuzzy comparison, plus identity attributes
rules.detection_logic: Pairs where name similarity exceeds threshold AND at least one identity attribute matches exactly
rules.threshold_parameter: Similarity threshold default 0.85. Identity match is mandatory, not optional.
rules.confidence_basis: Computed: identity attribute match strength multiplied by name similarity. Report both components.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both names, the similarity score, the matching identity attribute, and both CIs' full attribute sets.
rules.false_positive_guard: Sequentially named devices (SRV01, SRV02) with a shared attribute written in error. Never fire on name similarity alone.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 above confidence threshold, Lane 3 below
rules.cross_domain_link: Feeds D3; the confidence slider matters most here

rules.rule: De-dup tasks open beyond age threshold
rules.what_it_means: De-duplication tasks have been open beyond an age threshold with no action.
rules.why_it_matters: The platform already detected these duplicates and told someone. Nobody acted. Evidence of a governance gap rather than a detection gap, which is a different and often more uncomfortable conversation.
rules.source_tables_fields: CMDB de-duplication task table, creation dates, state
rules.detection_logic: Open de-dup tasks WHERE age > threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 90 days. Configurable.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on task age.
rules.evidence_to_show: Task list with age, assigned group, and the duplicate sets they cover.
rules.false_positive_guard: Tasks deliberately parked pending a migration.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — resolve the underlying duplicates, close the tasks

rules.rule: Identification rule using name-only criteria
rules.what_it_means: An identification rule uses name as its only matching criterion, with no serial, IP, MAC or correlation_id.
rules.why_it_matters: This rule guarantees duplicates. Any source reporting the same device with a slightly different name creates a new CI. It is the manufacturing defect behind most of Group 4, and fixing duplicates without fixing this is pure rework.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_identifier, cmdb_identifier_entry criterion attributes
rules.detection_logic: Identification rules whose entry criteria contain only name-type attributes
rules.threshold_parameter: Attribute classification (identity vs descriptive) configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — the criteria list contains an identity attribute or it does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: The rule, its entry criteria, the class set it governs, and the duplicate count in those classes attributable to it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Classes where no better attribute exists (some logical CIs). Verify no identity attribute is available before accepting.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — amended identifier as an update set, tested in sub-production first
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of CMDB-033 through CMDB-041

rules.rule: Principal class with no identification rule
rules.what_it_means: A principal class has no identification rule at all.
rules.why_it_matters: Every CI created in that class is created blind. IRE cannot match, so every discovery run and every integration write is a potential new record.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_identifier coverage vs principal class list
rules.detection_logic: Principal classes with no applicable identification rule, including inherited rules from parent classes
rules.threshold_parameter: Must account for inheritance — a parent class rule may cover the child
rules.confidence_basis: 100% after inheritance resolution.
rules.evidence_to_show: Class list with CI counts, duplicate counts, and the inherited rule chain showing where coverage stops.
rules.false_positive_guard: Class covered by a parent rule. Inheritance resolution must be correct or this rule produces false positives at scale.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of duplicates in the affected classes

rules.rule: IRE bypass rate above threshold
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of CI creates that bypass the Identification and Reconciliation Engine entirely, arriving by direct insert, script, or import without IRE processing.
rules.why_it_matters: The single most diagnostic number in the CMDB model. If a large share of creates bypass IRE, nothing you fix downstream will hold, because the bypass path keeps producing unmatched records.
rules.source_tables_fields: CI creation audit, IRE processing records, import set and script-created CI attribution
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(CIs created without IRE processing) / COUNT(all CIs created) in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 20%. Escalate above 40%.
rules.confidence_basis: Computed ratio. Attribution to specific bypass paths at 90%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio, trend, and a ranked list of the specific integrations, scripts or import sets responsible.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate bulk migration with IRE deliberately bypassed under a documented plan.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — route the bypass paths through IRE
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of duplicate creation rate CMDB-038

rules.rule: Rule with no independent criterion
rules.what_it_means: An identification rule has no independent criterion — every criterion is dependent on a related CI.
rules.why_it_matters: The rule cannot identify the CI on its own terms. Matching becomes contingent on the related CI being correct first, which cascades failure.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_identifier_entry, independent flag per entry
rules.detection_logic: Rules where no entry is marked independent
rules.threshold_parameter: Fixed: zero independent entries
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: The rule, all its entries with independence flags, and the class set affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely dependent CI types (a disk on a server) where dependence is correct by design.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2

rules.rule: CIs created bypassing IRE
rules.what_it_means: Individual CIs created without passing through IRE.
rules.why_it_matters: The per-record view of CMDB-046. Useful for identifying which specific records are unmatched candidates, and for quantifying the cleanup.
rules.source_tables_fields: CI creation attribution, IRE processing records
rules.detection_logic: CIs with no IRE processing record at creation
rules.threshold_parameter: Report count and list; the ratio is CMDB-046
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on processing record absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list with creating source, creation date, and whether a matching CI already existed at creation time.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate direct creates for logical CIs that IRE does not govern.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — merge where a match now exists

rules.rule: IRE error volume trending up
rules.what_it_means: IRE error volume and its trend over the observation window.
rules.why_it_matters: Errors mean records failed to identify. Each one is a potential duplicate or a lost update. A rising trend means the problem is accelerating.
rules.source_tables_fields: IRE error table, grouped by error type and class
rules.detection_logic: COUNT and trend of IRE errors, grouped by error type
rules.threshold_parameter: Threshold relative to CI create volume, not absolute
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on count. Trend confidence from window length.
rules.evidence_to_show: Error count by type, trend chart, most affected classes, and sample error payloads.
rules.false_positive_guard: A one-time bulk load producing a spike.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — fix the identification rules producing the errors

rules.rule: Entry order producing weak matches first
rules.what_it_means: Identification entry order places weak criteria before strong ones, so a weak match succeeds before a strong criterion is evaluated.
rules.why_it_matters: Produces false matches: two different devices merged because a weak criterion matched first. Worse than a missed match, because merging is hard to undo.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_identifier_entry order field and criterion strength
rules.detection_logic: Rules where a descriptive-attribute entry has lower order than an identity-attribute entry
rules.threshold_parameter: Attribute strength classification configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — strength classification is a judgement encoded in config.
rules.evidence_to_show: The rule, entry order, criterion attributes, and any evidence of incorrect merges.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate ordering for a class where the weak criterion is actually reliable.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2
rules.cross_domain_link: Can cause incorrect merges, the inverse of duplicates

rules.rule: Source stopped reporting but still trusted
rules.what_it_means: A registered source has stopped reporting, but its precedence is still active, so ServiceNow continues to trust data it is no longer receiving.
rules.why_it_matters: The CMDB holds the last thing a dead source said and treats it as authoritative, blocking live sources from correcting it. Silent and long-lived.
rules.source_tables_fields: Datasource last-seen timestamps, reconciliation precedence config
rules.detection_logic: Sources with precedence active WHERE last reported data is older than threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 30 days. Configurable per source type.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on last-seen arithmetic. Impact confidence from the count of attributes it blocks.
rules.evidence_to_show: Source, last data received, precedence config, and the attributes and CI count currently frozen by it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Source that legitimately reports infrequently (annual audit feed). Set per-source thresholds.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — precedence correction

rules.rule: Two or more sources claiming precedence on one attribute
rules.what_it_means: Two or more registered sources claim precedence for the same attribute on the same class.
rules.why_it_matters: Whichever source writes last wins, so the attribute value is non-deterministic. Two reports run an hour apart can legitimately differ.
rules.source_tables_fields: Reconciliation definition table, datasource precedence config
rules.detection_logic: Attribute plus class combinations with more than one source at the same precedence level
rules.threshold_parameter: Same-precedence collisions only; different levels are correct behaviour
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration overlap.
rules.evidence_to_show: Attribute, class, the competing sources, their precedence values, and recent value flip-flopping evidence from audit.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate equal-precedence with a documented tie-break elsewhere.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2

rules.rule: Reconciliation rule defined but source unregistered
rules.what_it_means: Reconciliation rules are defined for a source that is not registered as a datasource, so the rules never apply.
rules.why_it_matters: Configuration that looks correct and does nothing. The team believes precedence is governed and it is not.
rules.source_tables_fields: Reconciliation definition table, registered datasource list
rules.detection_logic: Reconciliation rules referencing a source name absent from the registered datasource list
rules.threshold_parameter: Exact and normalised name comparison
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on registration absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: The rules, the unregistered source name, and the registered source list for comparison.
rules.false_positive_guard: Source name mismatch between config and registration (typo). Same fix, different framing.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2

rules.rule: Source writing attributes without precedence
rules.what_it_means: A source is writing attributes for which it holds no precedence.
rules.why_it_matters: It overwrites authoritative data with unauthoritative data. The precedence model exists and is being ignored by this source.
rules.source_tables_fields: Attribute source attribution, precedence config
rules.detection_logic: Attribute writes from a source not holding precedence for that attribute and class
rules.threshold_parameter: Observation window configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — depends on write attribution accuracy.
rules.evidence_to_show: Source, attributes written, count, and the source that should hold precedence.
rules.false_positive_guard: Source added recently and precedence not yet configured. Check registration date.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2

rules.rule: Attributes with no source claiming precedence
rules.what_it_means: Attributes that no registered source claims precedence for.
rules.why_it_matters: Any source can write them, last write wins, and the value has no owner. Lower severity than a precedence collision because the failure is unowned rather than contested.
rules.source_tables_fields: Attribute list per class, precedence config
rules.detection_logic: Attributes written by any source WHERE no precedence entry exists
rules.threshold_parameter: Scope to attributes actually written by a source
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on config absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Attribute list by class, the sources writing them, and write frequency.
rules.false_positive_guard: Attributes only ever set manually, where precedence is not a meaningful concept.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2

rules.rule: Relationship count collapse within a window
rules.what_it_means: The number of relationships in a class or range has dropped sharply within a time window.
rules.why_it_matters: The earliest warning signal that discovery has broken. Relationships disappear silently when a source stops confirming them, and nobody notices until an outage needs the graph. In the router case this preceded the incident by 29 days.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci counts by class over snapshots, sys_audit on relationship deletion
rules.detection_logic: Relationship count per class per window; flag drops exceeding threshold percentage
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 15% drop in 30 days. Configurable per class.
rules.confidence_basis: Computed from snapshot deltas. Requires at least 2 snapshots; state the window.
rules.evidence_to_show: Count trend by class, the deletion events from audit, the deleting process, and the affected CI list.
rules.false_positive_guard: Planned decommission of a device population. Cross-check against change records in the window.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — restore from an independent topology source if one exists
rules.cross_domain_link: Caused by ITOM credential or discovery failure; causes impact analysis blindness

rules.rule: Reachability from Business Services below threshold
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of principal-class CIs reachable by graph traversal from any Business Service.
rules.why_it_matters: The honest headline number for whether the CMDB can answer 'what is affected'. Most estates sit between 20% and 45% and have never measured it. Everything else in Group 6 is detail underneath this one.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci adjacency, svc_ci_assoc, CSDM service classes
rules.detection_logic: Traverse from every Business Service downward to configured depth; count distinct principal CIs reached / total principal CIs
rules.threshold_parameter: Depth limit default 8. Threshold default 60%.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the traversal. Depth limit must be stated with the number.
rules.evidence_to_show: Reachability percentage, the traversal depth used, unreachable CI counts by class, and the tier at which traversal typically terminates.
rules.false_positive_guard: Estate deliberately models only critical services. Report scoped to modelled services if so.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 bulk relationship restoration plus Lane 3 CSDM structure
rules.cross_domain_link: The composite outcome of Group 6 and Group 11

rules.rule: Principal CI with no upstream and no downstream edge
rules.what_it_means: A principal-class CI has no relationships in either direction — no parent, no child, nothing.
rules.why_it_matters: The CI exists in isolation. It can never appear in an impact calculation, a dependency map, or a change conflict check. It is a record, not a model element.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci parent and child columns, principal class list
rules.detection_logic: Principal-class CIs with zero rows in cmdb_rel_ci as either parent or child
rules.threshold_parameter: Scope to classes expected to have relationships
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on edge absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list by class, creation source, last_discovered, and whether an independent topology source suggests edges.
rules.false_positive_guard: Standalone CIs that legitimately have no relationships (some logical or licence CIs). Scope by class.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where an evidence source supplies the edges, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Direct cause of impact analysis returning empty

rules.rule: Host class with no Runs on children
rules.what_it_means: A host-class CI has no 'Runs on' children — no applications, services or processes recorded as running on it.
rules.why_it_matters: The server exists but nothing is recorded as depending on it. Changes to it appear risk-free. Outages on it appear to affect nothing.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci filtered to Runs on/Runs type, host class list
rules.detection_logic: Host-class CIs with no child edge of Runs-on type
rules.threshold_parameter: Host class set configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on edge absence. Recommendation confidence from the evidence source supplying the missing children.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI, its class, any discovery-reported processes or software, and the independent topology or software inventory data.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely idle or spare hosts. Cross-check last_discovered and any software inventory.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where discovery or software inventory supplies evidence
rules.cross_domain_link: Breaks change risk and outage impact

rules.rule: Application with no host
rules.what_it_means: An application-class CI has no host relationship — it is not recorded as running anywhere.
rules.why_it_matters: The inverse of CMDB-059 and equally damaging. The application cannot be traced to infrastructure, so infrastructure events never reach it.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci, application class list
rules.detection_logic: Application-class CIs with no parent edge of hosting type
rules.threshold_parameter: Application class set configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on edge absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI, class, any discovery evidence of its host, and the service it supports.
rules.false_positive_guard: SaaS or externally hosted applications with no internal host. Maintain an external-hosting flag or class exclusion.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 with evidence, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Edges pointing at retired or inactive CIs
rules.what_it_means: Relationships point to CIs that are retired, decommissioned or inactive.
rules.why_it_matters: Traversal follows these edges and includes dead infrastructure in live impact results. The answer is not empty, it is wrong, which is worse.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci joined to both endpoints' lifecycle state
rules.detection_logic: Edges where either endpoint has install_status or operational_status in a retired or inactive set
rules.threshold_parameter: Retired state set read from the instance configuration
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on state check.
rules.evidence_to_show: Edge, both endpoints with states, the edge creation date and source, and whether the live endpoint has a valid alternative edge.
rules.false_positive_guard: Edge deliberately retained for historical impact analysis. Rare.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — retire the edge, snapshot held
rules.cross_domain_link: Corrupts impact analysis with false positives

rules.rule: Circular dependency chains
rules.what_it_means: Relationship chains form a cycle: A depends on B depends on C depends on A.
rules.why_it_matters: Traversal either loops indefinitely or terminates arbitrarily. Impact calculations either hang or truncate silently, and the truncation is invisible.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci adjacency, cycle detection
rules.detection_logic: Depth-first traversal per relationship type detecting back edges
rules.threshold_parameter: Per relationship type; some types legitimately permit cycles (peer-to-peer)
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on cycle detection. Whether the cycle is invalid depends on type semantics.
rules.evidence_to_show: The cycle path with all CIs and edge types, plus each edge's creation source and date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate bidirectional or peer relationships. Exclude symmetric relationship types.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — which edge to break is a judgement
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes traversal failure and silent truncation

rules.rule: Manual edges contradicted by discovery
rules.what_it_means: A manually created relationship is contradicted by discovery or an independent topology source.
rules.why_it_matters: Manual edges age badly and nobody revisits them. This rule finds the ones the infrastructure has since disproved. The router demo turned on exactly this shape.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci with creation source, discovery payloads, independent topology data
rules.detection_logic: Manual edges where an authoritative source reports a different relationship for the same CI and type
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires an independent corroborating source; do not fire on absence alone
rules.confidence_basis: Computed: source count agreeing against the edge, edge age, and creator activity status. Two sources agreeing plus stale manual edge yields 94%.
rules.evidence_to_show: The manual edge with creator and date, the contradicting source data, and the proposed correct edge.
rules.false_positive_guard: Manual edge documenting something discovery structurally cannot see (a logical or contractual dependency). Check edge type.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — retire the manual edge, create the evidenced one, both snapshotted
rules.cross_domain_link: The core remediation of the router demo

rules.rule: Edge type invalid for the class pair
rules.what_it_means: The relationship type used is not valid for the parent and child class pair according to the type's own descriptors.
rules.why_it_matters: Traversal rules and impact logic assume type semantics. An invalid pairing produces edges the graph cannot interpret correctly.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci, cmdb_rel_type parent and child descriptors, class hierarchy
rules.detection_logic: Edges where parent or child class falls outside the type's permitted class scope
rules.threshold_parameter: Permitted scope read from cmdb_rel_type, with hierarchy expansion
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — depends on how strictly the estate defines type scope.
rules.evidence_to_show: Edge, type, both classes, the type's permitted class descriptors, and the valid type SAOS would suggest.
rules.false_positive_guard: Estate uses generic types deliberately. Check whether type scoping is configured at all before firing.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where the correct type is unambiguous, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Direction reversed
rules.what_it_means: The relationship direction is inverted relative to the type definition: the child is recorded as the parent.
rules.why_it_matters: Traversal goes the wrong way. Impact propagates upward where it should propagate downward, producing backwards dependency results.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci, cmdb_rel_type semantics, class hierarchy expectations
rules.detection_logic: Edges where the class pair strongly indicates the inverse direction for that type
rules.threshold_parameter: Direction expectation matrix per type and class pair, configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 88% — direction inference from class pair is strong but not absolute.
rules.evidence_to_show: Edge as recorded, the expected direction, both classes, and comparable correctly-directed edges in the estate.
rules.false_positive_guard: Unusual but legitimate topologies. Require a clear class-pair expectation before firing.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — reverse the edge, snapshot held

rules.rule: Edges unconfirmed within the staleness window
rules.what_it_means: Relationships have not been confirmed by any source within the freshness window for their type.
rules.why_it_matters: The edge may be correct or may be a fossil. Unconfirmed edges accumulate and the graph slowly stops describing reality.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci with last-confirmed timestamps, source attribution
rules.detection_logic: Edges whose most recent confirmation by any source exceeds the type's freshness window
rules.threshold_parameter: Window per relationship type; default 30 days for discovery-maintained types
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on timestamp arithmetic. Whether the edge is wrong is a separate question.
rules.evidence_to_show: Edge, last confirmation date, confirming source, and whether the source is still active.
rules.false_positive_guard: Edge types no source confirms by design (manual logical dependencies). Scope to discovery-maintained types.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — review, not automatic deletion

rules.rule: Duplicate edges between the same pair
rules.what_it_means: The same relationship type exists more than once between the same CI pair.
rules.why_it_matters: Harmless individually, distorting in aggregate. Inflates relationship counts, skews class distribution baselines, and doubles traversal work.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci grouped by parent, child, type
rules.detection_logic: Groups with count > 1
rules.threshold_parameter: Exact triple match
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — exact duplicate triple.
rules.evidence_to_show: The duplicate edges with creation dates and sources, and the survivor SAOS would keep.
rules.false_positive_guard: None material.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — retain the earliest or best-sourced, retire the rest

rules.rule: Discovery coverage ratio below threshold
rules.what_it_means: The ratio of devices discovered to devices expected, derived from network topology, IP ranges and known infrastructure.
rules.why_it_matters: Answers whether discovery is seeing the estate at all. A high CMDB score over 40% of the infrastructure is not a good score.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_device_history, IP range definitions, network CI topology
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(distinct devices successfully discovered) / COUNT(devices expected from range and topology analysis)
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 85%. Expected count derivation must be shown.
rules.confidence_basis: Confidence depends on the expected-count derivation. State the method explicitly.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio, the expected-count derivation, ranges with the largest gaps, and the failure phase for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ranges legitimately excluded from discovery (DMZ, third-party managed).
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — ITOM remediation
rules.cross_domain_link: Directly causes CMDB-072, CMDB-073; owned by ITOM

rules.rule: last\_discovered beyond schedule interval
rules.what_it_means: last_discovered on CIs is older than the discovery schedule interval that covers them.
rules.why_it_matters: Discovery is configured to refresh these CIs and is not doing so. Every attribute and relationship on them is unverified since that date.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.last_discovered, discovery_schedule interval per covering range
rules.detection_logic: CIs where (now - last_discovered) > covering schedule interval x tolerance
rules.threshold_parameter: Tolerance default 2x interval. Per-class interval overrides supported.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on arithmetic. Cause attribution from discovery_device_history at 95%.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list with last_discovered, the covering schedule, its interval, and the device history showing where discovery failed.
rules.false_positive_guard: CIs from sources other than discovery carrying a discovery_source value in error.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — fix the ITOM cause, then Lane 1 rediscovery trigger
rules.cross_domain_link: Symptom of ITOM credential, MID or pattern failure

rules.rule: CI never discovered but carrying a discovery source
rules.what_it_means: A CI carries a discovery_source value but has no discovery record and has never been discovered.
rules.why_it_matters: The CI claims a provenance it does not have. Usually an integration writing a discovery_source value to appear authoritative, which then affects precedence decisions.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.discovery_source, first_discovered, last_discovered, discovery_device_history
rules.detection_logic: CIs with discovery_source set to a discovery value WHERE first_discovered is empty AND no device history exists
rules.threshold_parameter: Discovery source value set configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on record absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list, the claimed source, the absent discovery evidence, and the actual creating process from audit.
rules.false_positive_guard: Discovery history purged by retention policy. Check the retention window before firing.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — correct the source attribution

rules.rule: Ranges in network CIs with no matching discovery schedule
rules.what_it_means: IP ranges present in the network CI data have no corresponding discovery schedule range.
rules.why_it_matters: Infrastructure exists that discovery has never been told to look for. A structural blind spot rather than a failure.
rules.source_tables_fields: Network CI IP data, discovery_schedule ranges, IP range item table
rules.detection_logic: Subnets derived from network CIs MINUS subnets covered by active discovery ranges
rules.threshold_parameter: CIDR overlap analysis, not string matching
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on range arithmetic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Uncovered subnets with the CI counts and device types in each, plus the nearest existing range.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ranges deliberately out of scope. Maintain a documented exclusion list.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — schedule creation is an ITOM change
rules.cross_domain_link: ITOM-001 is the same finding from the ITOM side

rules.rule: Single-source CIs above threshold
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of CIs confirmed by only one source.
rules.why_it_matters: Single-sourced CIs have no corroboration. When that source fails, the CI silently goes stale with nothing to catch it. This is the structural fragility behind the router outage.
rules.source_tables_fields: Source attribution per CI, cmdb_metadata last-seen data
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(CIs with exactly one reporting source) / COUNT(all CIs in scope)
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 60%. Report by class.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio, subject to source attribution completeness.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio by class, the dominant single sources, and the CI count at risk if each source fails.
rules.false_positive_guard: Classes where a single source is legitimately definitive.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Predicts the blast radius of any single ITOM failure

rules.rule: No update of any kind since creation
rules.what_it_means: A CI has had no update of any kind — no discovery, no integration, no manual edit — since it was created.
rules.why_it_matters: Either it is inert and should be retired, or it is real and nothing is watching it. Both need resolution.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.sys_created_on vs sys_updated_on
rules.detection_logic: CIs where sys_updated_on equals sys_created_on (within tolerance) AND age exceeds threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 180 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on timestamp comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list with age, creating source, class, and any task references.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely static reference CIs.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — retire or bring under discovery

rules.rule: Updated only by scripts for N months
rules.what_it_means: A CI has been updated only by scripts or integrations, never by discovery or a human, for an extended period.
rules.why_it_matters: The CI is being maintained by something that may not have authoritative knowledge. Often an integration keeping a record alive that discovery no longer sees.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_audit updated_by analysis, discovery evidence
rules.detection_logic: CIs where all updates in the window are from script or integration users AND no discovery confirmation exists
rules.threshold_parameter: Window default 180 days
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on correct classification of updating users.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI list, the updating process, what it updates, and the absence of discovery confirmation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate integration-managed CI classes (cloud resources, SaaS).
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Suggests discovery gap masked by integration activity

rules.rule: Retired CI still holding active relationships
rules.what_it_means: A CI is marked retired but still holds active relationships.
rules.why_it_matters: Traversal includes decommissioned infrastructure in live results. Impact analysis returns a confident wrong answer that includes things that no longer exist.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci lifecycle fields, cmdb_rel_ci
rules.detection_logic: CIs in a retired state with one or more active edges
rules.threshold_parameter: Retired state set read from instance configuration
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on state and edge check.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI, its state, its edges, the connected CIs and their states, and the retirement date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Retirement in progress with a documented decommission change open.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — retire the edges, snapshot held

rules.rule: Retired CI still on an active service map
rules.what_it_means: A retired CI still appears on an active service map.
rules.why_it_matters: The service map asserts dependency on something decommissioned. Every impact calculation using that map is wrong, and service mapping will not self-correct because the CI is no longer discovered.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci lifecycle, svc_ci_assoc, service map data
rules.detection_logic: Retired-state CIs present in an active service map association
rules.threshold_parameter: Active map definition configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on state and association check.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI, state, the maps including it, the services affected, and the map's last refresh date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Map not refreshed since a legitimate recent retirement. Check retirement date against map refresh.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — remove from map, trigger remap

rules.rule: Decommissioned in asset, active in CMDB
rules.what_it_means: The asset record shows the item decommissioned or disposed while the CI shows it active, or the reverse.
rules.why_it_matters: Asset and CMDB disagree on whether the thing exists. Finance, audit and operations each read a different system and get a different answer.
rules.source_tables_fields: alm_asset / alm_hardware state, cmdb_ci lifecycle, asset-CI link
rules.detection_logic: Linked asset-CI pairs where lifecycle states are contradictory
rules.threshold_parameter: State mapping between asset and CI lifecycle models, configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — depends on the correctness of the state mapping.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both records, both states, the link, the last update on each, and the source of each update.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate lag during a decommission workflow. Check for an open decommission task.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — which record is right is an asset-management judgement
rules.cross_domain_link: Asset reconciliation; feeds Data Quality model

rules.rule: Deleted CI leaving orphaned relationships
rules.what_it_means: A CI has been deleted but its relationships remain, pointing at a record that no longer exists.
rules.why_it_matters: Traversal encounters a broken reference. Depending on the consumer this either errors or silently drops the branch, truncating impact results without warning.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci parent and child sys_ids vs cmdb_ci existence
rules.detection_logic: Edges where either endpoint sys_id has no corresponding CI record
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — the referenced record exists or it does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Orphaned edge, the missing sys_id, the surviving endpoint, and the deletion event from audit if retained.
rules.false_positive_guard: None. This is always a defect.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — delete the orphaned edge, snapshot held

rules.rule: Retired CI referenced by open incidents or changes
rules.what_it_means: A retired CI is still referenced by open incidents, changes or requests.
rules.why_it_matters: Work is being tracked against something that officially does not exist. Either the retirement was premature or the tasks were never reassigned.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci lifecycle, task tables referencing cmdb_ci
rules.detection_logic: Retired-state CIs with one or more open task references
rules.threshold_parameter: Open state set per task table
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on reference check.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI, state, retirement date, the open tasks with their ages and assignment groups.
rules.false_positive_guard: Tasks deliberately open to complete the decommission itself.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — task reassignment is an operational decision
rules.cross_domain_link: ITSM linkage; often reveals incomplete decommission

rules.rule: Lifecycle contradicting asset lifecycle
rules.what_it_means: CI lifecycle state contradicts the lifecycle recorded on its linked asset.
rules.why_it_matters: The narrower, record-level version of CMDB-082, scoped to lifecycle fields specifically rather than overall state.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci lifecycle fields, alm_asset lifecycle fields, link
rules.detection_logic: Linked pairs where lifecycle values map to different stages
rules.threshold_parameter: Mapping table between CI and asset lifecycle models
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — mapping-dependent.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both lifecycle values, the mapping, and the update history on each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate transitional lag.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Retirement backlog beyond threshold
rules.what_it_means: CIs flagged as stale beyond a threshold have had no retirement action taken.
rules.why_it_matters: Detection happened; action did not. The stale population grows and dilutes every other metric.
rules.source_tables_fields: Staleness flags or derived staleness, retirement task or state changes
rules.detection_logic: CIs stale beyond threshold with no retirement task and no state change
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 180 days stale with no action
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on arithmetic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by class, age distribution, and the owning groups.
rules.false_positive_guard: Retirement deliberately deferred pending a project.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 bulk state change

rules.rule: No lifecycle change since creation
rules.what_it_means: A CI's lifecycle state has never changed since creation despite significant age.
rules.why_it_matters: Suggests lifecycle is not being managed at all for that class. Weak individually, strong as a class-level ratio.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_audit on lifecycle fields, CI age
rules.detection_logic: CIs with no lifecycle field audit entry AND age above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 365 days. Report as a class ratio.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on audit absence. Report as a pattern, not per record.
rules.evidence_to_show: Percentage per class with no lifecycle change, and the age distribution.
rules.false_positive_guard: Long-lived infrastructure legitimately in one state.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Support group with zero active members
rules.what_it_means: The support group assigned to a CI has zero active members.
rules.why_it_matters: The most valuable ownership finding in the set, because it exposes the metric itself as false. The dashboard reports ownership complete; at two in the morning there is nobody to call. Report nominal and effective ownership separately and show the gap.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.support_group, sys_user_grmember, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: CIs whose support group resolves to zero active members at evaluation time
rules.threshold_parameter: Active membership resolved live, not from the group record
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — membership resolves to a person or it does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI count by group, the empty groups, their last membership change date, and the Business Critical services affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Group deliberately empty pending a transition, with a documented interim owner elsewhere.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — reassignment is an ownership decision, then Lane 1 bulk apply
rules.cross_domain_link: Cross-links to Data Quality Q2; invalidates D9 nominal completeness

rules.rule: Owner is an inactive user
rules.what_it_means: The CI owner is an inactive user.
rules.why_it_matters: Notifications, approvals and escalations routed to this owner go nowhere. The field is populated, so every completeness metric counts it as a pass.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci.owned_by, managed_by, assigned_to; sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: CIs whose owner reference resolves to a user with active=false
rules.threshold_parameter: Evaluate all ownership fields in use on the class
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on user state.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI count by inactive owner, the owner's deactivation date, and the CIs' criticality.
rules.false_positive_guard: User deactivated within a grace period with a documented successor.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where a successor is inferable from group or manager, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Classes with no defined data owner
rules.what_it_means: CI classes have no defined data owner at the class level — nobody is accountable for the quality of that class.
rules.why_it_matters: Without class ownership there is no path to remediation. Findings have no recipient, and every improvement effort stalls at the question of whose job it is.
rules.source_tables_fields: Data Manager class ownership configuration, principal class list
rules.detection_logic: Principal classes with no class-level data owner configured
rules.threshold_parameter: Fixed: absence of configuration
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Class list with CI counts, defect counts, and absence of owner, ranked by defect volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ownership held in an external RACI with documented evidence.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Blocks remediation of every other finding in that class

rules.rule: No owner, manager or support group
rules.what_it_means: A CI has no owner, no managed_by and no support group — no accountability reference of any kind.
rules.why_it_matters: Nobody owns it. Incidents against it cannot route, changes cannot be approved by an owner, and no attestation can be assigned.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci ownership fields
rules.detection_logic: CIs where all configured ownership fields are empty
rules.threshold_parameter: Field set per class
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on emptiness.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI count by class, with any inferable owner signal: incident assignment history, change approver history, parent service owner.
rules.false_positive_guard: Classes where ownership is genuinely held at the service level rather than the CI level.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where strongly inferable from history, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Ownership inconsistent with parent application service
rules.what_it_means: A CI's ownership differs from the ownership of the application service it supports.
rules.why_it_matters: Not automatically wrong, but it means escalation paths diverge. During an incident, two different groups believe they own the response, or neither does.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci ownership, application service ownership, svc_ci_assoc and cmdb_rel_ci
rules.detection_logic: CIs whose owner or support group differs from that of their supporting application service
rules.threshold_parameter: Report as a ratio per service before raising individual findings
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — divergence is a signal, not proof of error.
rules.evidence_to_show: The CI, the service, both ownership sets, and the incident routing history for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate separation between infrastructure ownership and service ownership. Confirm the estate's convention.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Single owner holding a disproportionate share
rules.what_it_means: A single user or group owns a disproportionate share of the CI estate.
rules.why_it_matters: Concentration risk. Usually indicates bulk assignment during migration rather than real ownership, and it creates a single point of failure in the accountability model.
rules.source_tables_fields: Ownership field distribution
rules.detection_logic: Owners holding more than N percent of CIs in scope
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 20% of the in-scope estate. Report distribution regardless.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on distribution. The judgement that it is wrong is advisory.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ownership distribution chart, top owners with counts, and the assignment date pattern.
rules.false_positive_guard: A genuinely centralised infrastructure team.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Impact analysis success rate below threshold
rules.what_it_means: The impact analysis success rate — the percentage of alerts and changes where the affected-service calculation returns a non-empty result.
rules.why_it_matters: The closest thing to a single honest measure of whether the CMDB works. Every other dimension is an input; this is the output. It is exactly what failed on 14 March, and no dashboard in the platform produces it.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert impact results, change_request affected service calculation results, bound CI relationship state
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(alerts and changes returning a non-empty affected-service result) / COUNT(alerts and changes with a CI reference)
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 70%. Report alerts and changes separately as well as combined.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio. Per-record cause attribution computed from the CI edge state and duplicate membership.
rules.evidence_to_show: The ratio for alerts and for changes, trended, with per-record cause breakdown: zero edges, duplicate binding, no path to a service, or CI class outside the impact model.
rules.false_positive_guard: Alerts and changes on CI classes deliberately outside the service model. Scope the denominator accordingly.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 for CI-level causes, Lane 3 for CSDM structural causes
