rules.cross_domain_link: The outcome measure for the entire CMDB Quality model

rules.rule: Incidents referencing a Business Service, percentage
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of incidents that reference a Business Service rather than a bare CI or nothing at all.
rules.why_it_matters: Measures whether the service model is actually used by the process that most needs it. Low values mean incidents cannot be aggregated by service, and service-level reporting is fiction.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.business_service, incident volume
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(incidents with business_service populated) / COUNT(incidents) in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 60%. Window default 90 days.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio trend, distribution by assignment group, and the services that do get referenced for contrast.
rules.false_positive_guard: Estate does not use service-based incident management by design.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — form and process configuration
rules.cross_domain_link: ITSM linkage; proves or disproves CMDB consumption

rules.rule: Incidents referencing any CI, percentage
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of incidents that reference any CI at all.
rules.why_it_matters: The most basic consumption measure. If incidents do not reference CIs, the CMDB is not part of the operational workflow regardless of how healthy it is.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.cmdb_ci, incident volume
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(incidents with cmdb_ci populated) / COUNT(incidents) in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 50%
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio trend, distribution by category and group, and the classes most referenced.
rules.false_positive_guard: Service-desk categories where CI reference is not meaningful (HR, facilities).
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2

rules.rule: Custom classes duplicating OOB
rules.what_it_means: Custom CI classes duplicate the function of an existing out-of-box class.
rules.why_it_matters: Splits the estate across two classes for the same thing. Identification rules, health rules and relationship rules apply to one and not the other, so half the population is ungoverned.
rules.source_tables_fields: Custom class definitions, attribute profiles, OOB class profiles
rules.detection_logic: Custom classes whose attribute signature substantially overlaps an OOB class, with both populated
rules.threshold_parameter: Overlap threshold configurable; require both classes populated
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — signature overlap is a strong but not conclusive indicator.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both classes, their attribute profiles, row counts, and the overlap percentage.
rules.false_positive_guard: Custom class with a genuinely distinct purpose despite attribute overlap.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — class consolidation is an architecture decision

rules.rule: CIs never referenced by any task in 12 months
rules.what_it_means: CIs that have not been referenced by any task — incident, change, problem, request — in twelve months.
rules.why_it_matters: Either the CI is genuinely inert, or the processes are not using the CMDB. Both are worth knowing, and the distinction is made by comparing this against overall consumption rates.
rules.source_tables_fields: Task tables referencing cmdb_ci, CI list
rules.detection_logic: CIs with zero task references in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Window default 365 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on reference absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by class, contrasted against the overall incident CI-reference rate to distinguish inert CIs from unused CMDB.
rules.false_positive_guard: Infrastructure that legitimately never generates tickets.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Retirement candidate population and consumption signal

rules.rule: Classes with fewer than five records
rules.what_it_means: CI classes containing fewer than five records.
rules.why_it_matters: Almost always a modelling mistake: a class created for a purpose that never materialised, or records that belong in a broader class. Adds governance surface with no benefit.
rules.source_tables_fields: Row counts per CMDB class
rules.detection_logic: Classes with row count between 1 and 5
rules.threshold_parameter: Threshold configurable, default 5
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on count.
rules.evidence_to_show: Class list with row counts, creation dates, and the records themselves.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely rare CI types (a mainframe, a single specialised appliance).
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Extension depth beyond recommended
rules.what_it_means: CI class extension depth exceeds the recommended maximum.
rules.why_it_matters: Deep extension chains make attribute inheritance hard to reason about and slow class-based queries. A maintainability and performance signal rather than a correctness one.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_db_object super_class chain within the CMDB tree
rules.detection_logic: Classes whose extension depth from cmdb_ci exceeds threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 6 levels
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on depth arithmetic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Class hierarchy diagram with depth, row counts at each level, and the custom levels highlighted.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deep OOB hierarchies that ServiceNow itself ships.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Group with no manager and no email
rules.what_it_means: A group has no manager and no email address.
rules.why_it_matters: Escalation from that group has no destination and notifications to it go nowhere. The group functions for assignment and fails for everything else.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_group manager and email fields
rules.detection_logic: Active groups with empty manager AND empty email
rules.threshold_parameter: Both absent; escalate where the group is referenced by open tasks
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Group list with member count, the open tasks assigned to each, and the notification rules targeting them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Groups used purely as role containers with no operational assignment.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — assignment is an ownership decision
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes notification and escalation failure across ITSM

rules.rule: Location with no country or timezone where routing depends on it
rules.what_it_means: A location record has no country or timezone where routing or SLA logic depends on those fields.
rules.why_it_matters: SLA schedules resolve to the wrong timezone and location-based routing falls to a default. A four-hour target measured in the wrong timezone breaches or passes for the wrong reasons.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_location country and timezone fields, SLA schedules and routing rules referencing location
rules.detection_logic: Locations with empty country or timezone that are referenced by CIs, users, or SLA and routing rules
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires only where rules reference the field
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state and rule reference.
rules.evidence_to_show: Location list with referencing record counts, the rules that evaluate the empty field, and the SLA schedules affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Locations not used in any timezone-sensitive logic.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where inferable from parent location, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Corrupts SLA calculation and location routing

rules.rule: Asset with no model or serial
rules.what_it_means: An asset record has no model or no serial number.
rules.why_it_matters: Asset-to-CI reconciliation cannot match, warranty and lifecycle tracking cannot function, and the asset cannot be identified physically.
rules.source_tables_fields: alm_asset and alm_hardware model_id and serial_number fields
rules.detection_logic: Assets with empty model_id or empty serial_number
rules.threshold_parameter: Report the two cases separately; escalate where both are absent
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Asset count by class and state, their cost where recorded, and the CI linkage state for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Asset classes where serial is not applicable, such as consumables or licences.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: User with no manager (approval chains cannot resolve)
rules.what_it_means: A user record has no manager.
rules.why_it_matters: Any approval chain that resolves through the manager hierarchy fails. Requests hang with no visible cause, because the approval was never created rather than never actioned.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user manager field, approval workflows referencing manager
rules.detection_logic: Active users with empty manager, joined to the approval workflows that would resolve through them
rules.threshold_parameter: Escalate for users who submit requests requiring manager approval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: User count, their departments, the approval workflows that resolve through manager, and the requests currently hanging.
rules.false_positive_guard: Users at the top of the hierarchy, and service accounts.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — sourced from HR, not guessed

rules.rule: Cost centre with no account number
rules.what_it_means: A cost centre has no account number.
rules.why_it_matters: Financial integration and chargeback cannot resolve the cost centre to a ledger account. Costs are allocated to a label with no financial meaning.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_cost_center account number field
rules.detection_logic: Active cost centres with empty account number
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence where financial integration exists
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Cost centre list with the CIs, assets and users allocated to each, and the financial integration state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Cost centres not used for financial allocation.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: User with no department, location or company
rules.what_it_means: A user record has no department, location or company.
rules.why_it_matters: Routing, reporting and entitlement all key off these fields. Their absence means the user is invisible to every organisational view.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user department, location, company fields
rules.detection_logic: Active users with any of the three empty
rules.threshold_parameter: Report per field; escalate where all three are absent
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: User count per missing field, the routing rules that evaluate them, and the incident volume from those users.
rules.false_positive_guard: Contractors or external users where organisational data is deliberately absent.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — sourced from HR

rules.rule: Group with no type defined
rules.what_it_means: A group has no type defined.
rules.why_it_matters: Group type drives which processes can use the group — approval, assignment, catalog fulfilment, change approval. An untyped group may be usable in contexts it was never intended for.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_group type field
rules.detection_logic: Active groups with empty type
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Group list with member counts, the contexts each is currently used in, and the types those contexts require.
rules.false_positive_guard: Estates that do not use group typing.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where the usage pattern determines the type, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Catalog item with no owner or fulfilment group
rules.what_it_means: A catalog item has no owner or no fulfilment group.
rules.why_it_matters: Requests against the item have nowhere to go, or nobody to maintain it. Requests submitted against an unfulfillable item hang and are eventually cancelled.
rules.source_tables_fields: sc_cat_item owner and fulfilment group fields
rules.detection_logic: Active catalog items with empty owner or empty fulfilment group
rules.threshold_parameter: Report the two separately; escalate on fulfilment group
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Item list with order volume, the requests currently open against each, and their ages.
rules.false_positive_guard: Items fulfilled by a workflow that assigns dynamically.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Location with no parent in the hierarchy
rules.what_it_means: A location has no parent in the hierarchy.
rules.why_it_matters: The hierarchy is broken at that node. Roll-up reporting excludes everything beneath it, and hierarchical routing cannot traverse past it.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_location parent field, hierarchy traversal
rules.detection_logic: Locations with empty parent that are not intended roots
rules.threshold_parameter: Root locations identified by configuration or by depth
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state and root identification.
rules.evidence_to_show: Location list, their depth, the CIs and users beneath them, and the roll-up reporting that excludes them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate root locations.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where the parent is inferable from address or naming, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Model with no manufacturer
rules.what_it_means: A model record has no manufacturer.
rules.why_it_matters: Model normalisation and software or hardware lifecycle tracking cannot group by vendor. Duplicate models proliferate because there is no manufacturer to disambiguate by.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_model manufacturer field
rules.detection_logic: Active models with empty manufacturer
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Model list with the asset and CI counts using each, and the duplicate model candidates that manufacturer would disambiguate.
rules.false_positive_guard: Generic or internal models with no manufacturer.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where inferable from model name, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Knowledge article with no owner or review date
rules.what_it_means: A knowledge article has no owner or no review date.
rules.why_it_matters: Nobody is responsible for keeping it accurate and nothing prompts a review. The article ages indefinitely while remaining published and consumed.
rules.source_tables_fields: kb_knowledge owner and review date fields
rules.detection_logic: Published articles with empty owner or empty review date
rules.threshold_parameter: Report the two separately
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Article list with view counts, publication date, age, and the incidents citing them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Articles under an external review process.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Approver or manager is an inactive user
rules.what_it_means: An approver or manager reference resolves to an inactive user.
rules.why_it_matters: The approval chain terminates at somebody who has left. The request does not fail — it waits, indefinitely, with no error anywhere.
rules.source_tables_fields: Approval configuration, sys_user.manager, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: Approval and manager references resolving to users with active=false
rules.threshold_parameter: Evaluate across approval definitions, delegations and manager chains
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — the reference resolves to an active user or does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: The references, the inactive users with deactivation dates, the pending approvals blocked, and their ages.
rules.false_positive_guard: User deactivated within a grace period with a delegate configured.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: The single most common cause of silently hanging approvals

rules.rule: Group assigned as approver with zero active members
rules.what_it_means: A group assigned as an approver has zero active members.
rules.why_it_matters: Group approval requires a member to act. With none, the approval can never be granted and the request never completes.
rules.source_tables_fields: Approval configuration referencing groups, sys_user_grmember, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: Approver groups resolving to zero active members
rules.threshold_parameter: Active membership resolved live at evaluation time
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — resolves to a member or does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Group, its membership history, the approvals pending on it, their ages, and the requests blocked.
rules.false_positive_guard: Group emptied with reassignment in progress.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Email failing format validation on notification-critical records
rules.what_it_means: Email addresses fail format validation on records that notifications depend on.
rules.why_it_matters: The notification is generated and the delivery fails. Notification logs record the attempt, so the process appears to have run.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user and sys_user_group email fields, format validation
rules.detection_logic: Email values failing RFC format validation on records referenced by active notification rules
rules.threshold_parameter: Scope to notification-referenced records
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — format validation catches malformed addresses, not wrong-but-valid ones.
rules.evidence_to_show: Record list with the malformed value pattern, the notification rules targeting them, and the delivery failure counts.
rules.false_positive_guard: Valid but unusual address formats. Use a permissive validator.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Choice value in use that is absent from sys\_choice
rules.what_it_means: A field holds a choice value that is not present in its sys_choice list.
rules.why_it_matters: Arrived by import or API, bypassing UI validation. Reporting grouped on the field splits across phantom values and any logic switching on the choice falls through.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_choice per table and element, actual field values
rules.detection_logic: Field values not present in the active sys_choice set, with inheritance from parent tables resolved
rules.threshold_parameter: Include inactive choices as a separate case
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — the value is in the list or it is not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Field, the invalid values with counts, the valid choice list, and the source writing them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Recently retired choices still held by historical records. Scope to active records.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where mapping is unambiguous, Lane 2 for the validation gap
rules.cross_domain_link: Indicates an import or integration bypassing validation

rules.rule: Asset state contradicting its linked CI state
rules.what_it_means: An asset's state contradicts the state of its linked CI.
rules.why_it_matters: Finance and operations read different systems and get different answers about whether the item exists. Both are authoritative for their own purpose and they disagree.
rules.source_tables_fields: alm_asset state, cmdb_ci lifecycle, asset-CI link, state mapping
rules.detection_logic: Linked asset-CI pairs whose states map to contradictory lifecycle stages
rules.threshold_parameter: Mapping table between asset and CI state models, configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — depends on the state mapping being correct for this estate.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both records with states, the link, last update and updating source on each, and the mapping applied.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate transitional lag during a decommission workflow.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — which record is right is an asset management judgement

rules.rule: Manager pointing to self
rules.what_it_means: A user's manager field points to the user themselves.
rules.why_it_matters: The approval chain loops immediately. Usually a data entry artefact, occasionally a deliberate workaround for a missing manager.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user manager field
rules.detection_logic: Users where manager equals sys_id
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — direct comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: User list, their department, and the approval workflows that resolve through manager.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate for executives at the top of the hierarchy.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Phone number not conforming to a defined pattern
rules.what_it_means: Phone numbers do not conform to a defined format pattern.
rules.why_it_matters: Affects notification by SMS or voice and directory usability. Lowest severity in the group because the consequence is contained.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user phone and mobile fields, format patterns
rules.detection_logic: Phone values failing the configured pattern set
rules.threshold_parameter: Pattern set per region; for India include the standard mobile and landline formats
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — international variation makes strict validation error-prone.
rules.evidence_to_show: Value patterns with counts, the expected patterns, and the notification rules using them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate international formats not in the pattern set.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Contained; affects SMS and voice notification

rules.rule: Model class contradicting the CI class it maps to
rules.what_it_means: A model's class contradicts the class of the CI it maps to.
rules.why_it_matters: Model-driven normalisation assigns the wrong class, or the CI was reclassified and the model was not. Produces class inconsistency that propagates to every class-scoped rule.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_model class, linked CI sys_class_name
rules.detection_logic: Model-CI pairs whose classes are inconsistent per the model class mapping
rules.threshold_parameter: Mapping configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on the model-to-class mapping convention in this estate.
rules.evidence_to_show: Model, its class, the CIs linked with their classes, and the counts for each mismatch pair.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate use of a generic model across related classes.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Manager chain containing a loop
rules.what_it_means: The manager chain contains a loop — following manager references returns to a user already in the chain.
rules.why_it_matters: Any approval or escalation traversing the hierarchy runs indefinitely or terminates arbitrarily. Where it terminates determines who approves, and that is effectively random.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user manager references, cycle detection
rules.detection_logic: Depth-first traversal of manager references detecting back edges
rules.threshold_parameter: Depth limit configurable as a safety bound
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on cycle detection.
rules.evidence_to_show: The loop path with all users, their departments, and the approval workflows that traverse manager.
rules.false_positive_guard: None. A manager loop is always a defect.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — correction requires HR authority

rules.rule: Location hierarchy containing a cycle
rules.what_it_means: The location hierarchy contains a cycle.
rules.why_it_matters: Roll-up reporting loops or truncates. Location-based traversal cannot terminate, and the truncation point is arbitrary.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_location parent references, cycle detection
rules.detection_logic: Depth-first traversal of location parents detecting back edges
rules.threshold_parameter: Depth limit as a safety bound
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on cycle detection.
rules.evidence_to_show: The cycle path, the locations involved, and the CIs and users beneath each.
rules.false_positive_guard: None.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — break the cycle at the least-evidenced edge, reversible

rules.rule: User's department belonging to a different company than the user
rules.what_it_means: A user's department belongs to a different company than the user.
rules.why_it_matters: In a group structure this means the organisational hierarchy contradicts itself. Reporting by company and by department produce different populations.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user company and department, cmn_department company
rules.detection_logic: Users whose company differs from the company on their department
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires only on multi-company instances
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: User count by mismatch pair, the departments and companies involved, and which of the two is more consistently populated elsewhere.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate cross-entity secondments.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Group members drawn from companies the group does not serve
rules.what_it_means: Group members are drawn from companies the group does not serve.
rules.why_it_matters: Access and assignment cross an entity boundary. In a regulated group structure this can be a segregation concern rather than a data one.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_group company, sys_user_grmember, member company
rules.detection_logic: Groups whose members include users from companies outside the group's company scope
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires only on multi-company instances with group company scoping in use
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Group, its company, the out-of-scope members and their companies, and what the group grants.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate shared-services groups spanning entities.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — escalate to access review in regulated entities
rules.cross_domain_link: Potential segregation finding in group structures

rules.rule: Asset assigned to one user, linked CI assigned to another
rules.what_it_means: An asset is assigned to one user while its linked CI is assigned to another.
rules.why_it_matters: Two systems disagree about who has the item. Recovery, recertification and chargeback each pick a different answer.
rules.source_tables_fields: alm_asset assigned_to, cmdb_ci assigned_to, asset-CI link
rules.detection_logic: Linked pairs with differing assigned_to values, both populated
rules.threshold_parameter: Both populated and different
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both records, both assignees, last update and source on each, and the asset cost.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate distinction between custodian and user.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Naming conventions diverging between import-created and manually created records
rules.what_it_means: Naming conventions diverge between records created by import and records created manually.
rules.why_it_matters: Two populations that look like different things and are the same. Fuzzy duplicate detection degrades, and human search misses half the estate.
rules.source_tables_fields: Record names by creation source, pattern frequency analysis
rules.detection_logic: Name pattern distribution split by creation source; flag divergence above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires a dominant pattern in at least one population
rules.confidence_basis: 75% — convention inference is probabilistic. Report as a ratio with samples.
rules.evidence_to_show: Pattern distribution by source, sample names from each, and the duplicate candidates the divergence conceals.
rules.false_positive_guard: Multiple legitimate conventions by region or entity.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Hierarchy depth varying widely across regions
rules.what_it_means: Hierarchy depth varies widely across regions in the location or department structure.
rules.why_it_matters: Roll-up reporting compares nodes at different levels. A regional total and a site total appear side by side as peers.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_location and cmn_department hierarchy depth by branch
rules.detection_logic: Depth variance across top-level branches beyond threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Variance threshold configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on depth measurement.
rules.evidence_to_show: Depth by branch, the record counts at each level, and the reports that group across branches.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely different organisational structures by region.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Cost centre pointing at a company that does not own it
rules.what_it_means: A cost centre points at a company that does not own it.
rules.why_it_matters: Financial allocation crosses an entity boundary. In a group structure this is a reporting error with financial consequence.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_cost_center company field, company ownership structure
rules.detection_logic: Cost centres whose company reference is inconsistent with their account or parent structure
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires only on multi-company instances
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on the ownership structure being derivable.
rules.evidence_to_show: Cost centre, its company, its parent and account structure, and the allocations flowing through it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate shared cost centres.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Duplicate users by email or employee number
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate user records exist, matched by email address or employee number.
rules.why_it_matters: Assignments, approvals and entitlements split across two identities. One record has the roles, the other receives the notifications, and neither works completely.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user email and employee_number, duplicate detection
rules.detection_logic: User records sharing an email address or employee number, excluding inactive-to-active supersession pairs
rules.threshold_parameter: Report active-active pairs separately from active-inactive
rules.confidence_basis: 97% on employee number match, 95% on email match.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both records with their roles, group memberships, open tasks, last login, and creation source.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate second account for a different function, such as an admin account.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — user merge has entitlement consequences
rules.cross_domain_link: Splits entitlement and notification across identities

rules.rule: Duplicate groups with identical membership
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate groups exist with identical or near-identical membership.
rules.why_it_matters: Assignment and approval routing split across two groups serving the same people. Which group a record reaches is arbitrary.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_group records, sys_user_grmember set comparison
rules.detection_logic: Group pairs whose active membership sets overlap above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Overlap threshold default 90%; minimum membership 3
rules.confidence_basis: Membership overlap is exact; the conclusion that they are duplicates is inferred at 85%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both groups, their membership sets, their roles, the tasks assigned to each, and their creation dates.
rules.false_positive_guard: Groups with identical membership serving genuinely different functions.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Duplicate locations by address
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate location records exist, matched by address.
rules.why_it_matters: CIs and users at the same physical place are recorded at two different locations. Site-level reporting and DR scoping split.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_location address fields, normalised comparison
rules.detection_logic: Location records with matching normalised address
rules.threshold_parameter: Address normalisation configurable; include postcode where available
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — address matching is sensitive to formatting variance.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both locations, their addresses, the CIs and users assigned to each, and their hierarchy positions.
rules.false_positive_guard: Distinct facilities at the same address, such as separate floors or buildings.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Splits site-level reporting and DR scoping

rules.rule: Duplicate companies
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate company records exist.
rules.why_it_matters: Entity-level reporting splits. On a multi-company instance this affects domain separation, financial allocation and regulatory reporting simultaneously.
rules.source_tables_fields: core_company records, name and identifier comparison
rules.detection_logic: Company records with matching normalised name or registration identifier
rules.threshold_parameter: Include registration number where populated
rules.confidence_basis: 95% on identifier match, 85% on name match alone.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both records, their identifiers, the users, CIs and cost centres assigned to each, and domain configuration.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legally distinct entities with similar names.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — company merge affects domain separation

rules.rule: Duplicate models by manufacturer and part number
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate model records exist, matched by manufacturer and part number.
rules.why_it_matters: Model-driven normalisation, lifecycle tracking and procurement reporting all split across the duplicates.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_model manufacturer and part number fields
rules.detection_logic: Model records with matching manufacturer and part number, normalised
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires manufacturer populated; DQ-093 gates this rule
rules.confidence_basis: 93% on manufacturer plus part number match.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both models, their attributes, the assets and CIs linked to each, and creation sources.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuine variants sharing a part number.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — model merge is low risk and reversible

rules.rule: Duplicate catalog items
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate catalog items exist.
rules.why_it_matters: Requesters see two routes to the same thing with potentially different fulfilment and approval. Demand data splits across both.
rules.source_tables_fields: sc_cat_item name and variable set comparison
rules.detection_logic: Catalog items with matching normalised name or identical variable sets and fulfilment
rules.threshold_parameter: Name normalisation plus variable set comparison
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — catalog items can legitimately be similar.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both items, their categories, variable sets, fulfilment groups, approval workflows, and order volumes.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate variants for different audiences or entities.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Splits demand data and creates inconsistent fulfilment

rules.rule: User inactive in the HR feed but active in ServiceNow
rules.what_it_means: A user is inactive in the HR feed but remains active in ServiceNow.
rules.why_it_matters: A leaver retains access. This is an access control finding before it is a data quality one, and in a regulated entity it is an audit exception.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user.active, HR feed import data, last import timestamps
rules.detection_logic: Active ServiceNow users absent from or marked inactive in the most recent successful HR feed
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires a successful recent HR import; guard on DQ-118
rules.confidence_basis: 95% where the HR import succeeded. Unusable if it failed — the guard is mandatory.
rules.evidence_to_show: User list, HR feed status, their roles and group memberships, last login, and the access each retains.
rules.false_positive_guard: Contractors and non-employees legitimately absent from the HR feed. Scope by user type.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — deactivation is an access decision requiring HR confirmation
rules.cross_domain_link: Access control finding; route to security review

rules.rule: HR feed failing or not run within interval
rules.what_it_means: The HR feed is failing, or has not run within its interval.
rules.why_it_matters: Joiner, mover and leaver data stops flowing. New users are absent, leavers retain access, and organisational data ages. One integration failure degrades identity, routing and access simultaneously.
rules.source_tables_fields: HR import set and data source run history, last successful import
rules.detection_logic: HR data source with error state, or last successful import beyond interval x tolerance
rules.threshold_parameter: Tolerance default 2x interval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on run history and timestamps.
rules.evidence_to_show: Data source, last successful run, error class, the user record delta accumulating since, and the leavers still active.
rules.false_positive_guard: Feed deliberately paused during an HR system migration.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of DQ-117, DQ-089, DQ-087

rules.rule: Active user who has never logged in
rules.what_it_means: An active user has never logged in.
rules.why_it_matters: Either the account was provisioned unnecessarily, or somebody has access they have never used. Both are licence cost and access surface.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user.active, last_login_time, creation date
rules.detection_logic: Active users with no login record and age above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 90 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on login record absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: User list with creation date, provisioning source, roles held, and licence consumption where applicable.
rules.false_positive_guard: Users who only receive notifications and never log in, such as approvers using email approval.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Group membership unchanged for over two years
rules.what_it_means: Group membership has not changed in over two years.
rules.why_it_matters: Membership has not been reviewed through any organisational change in that period. Access recertification, if it exists, is not reaching this group.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_grmember audit history, group age
rules.detection_logic: Groups with no membership change beyond age threshold, with active membership
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 730 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on audit history.
rules.evidence_to_show: Group list, membership count, last change date, the roles the group grants, and the recertification state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely stable teams.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Asset past end-of-life still in Deployed state
rules.what_it_means: An asset is past its end-of-life date and still in a Deployed state.
rules.why_it_matters: Unsupported equipment in production. Warranty has expired, vendor support is unavailable, and the risk is unrecorded.
rules.source_tables_fields: alm_asset end-of-life and warranty dates, asset state
rules.detection_logic: Assets with end-of-life date in the past and state Deployed or In Use
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires end-of-life data to be populated
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on date and state arithmetic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Asset list with end-of-life date, days past, linked CI, the services those CIs support, and cost.
rules.false_positive_guard: Extended support contract in place not reflected in the record.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Knowledge article past its review date
rules.what_it_means: A knowledge article is past its review date.
rules.why_it_matters: Guidance being followed that nobody has confirmed is still correct. Every incident resolved using it inherits the risk.
rules.source_tables_fields: kb_knowledge review date, publication state, view counts
rules.detection_logic: Published articles with review date in the past
rules.threshold_parameter: Report by days overdue and by view volume
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on date arithmetic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Article list with review date, days overdue, view count since the review date, and the incidents citing them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Articles reviewed outside ServiceNow without updating the field.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Stale guidance in active use; joins ITSM-139

rules.rule: Catalog item never ordered
rules.what_it_means: A catalog item has never been ordered.
rules.why_it_matters: Catalogue clutter. Adds maintenance surface and makes the catalogue harder to navigate, which suppresses use of the items that matter.
rules.source_tables_fields: sc_cat_item, request item order history
rules.detection_logic: Active catalog items with zero orders and age above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 365 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on order history.
rules.evidence_to_show: Item list with creation date, category, owner, and the categories with the highest unused item counts.
rules.false_positive_guard: Seasonal or emergency items retained deliberately.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Location with no users and no CIs
rules.what_it_means: A location has no users and no CIs assigned to it.
rules.why_it_matters: An empty node in the hierarchy. Harmless in itself, but it inflates location pick lists and obscures the locations that are real.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_location, CI and user location references
rules.detection_logic: Active locations with zero CI and zero user references
rules.threshold_parameter: Exclude parent nodes with populated children
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on reference counts.
rules.evidence_to_show: Location list with hierarchy position, creation date, and children.
rules.false_positive_guard: Newly created locations ahead of a site opening, and structural parent nodes.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Task assignment group that no longer exists
rules.what_it_means: A task references an assignment group that no longer exists.
rules.why_it_matters: The reference is broken, not merely empty. The task shows a group that cannot be opened, and it appears in no group's queue.
rules.source_tables_fields: Task assignment_group sys_ids, sys_user_group existence
rules.detection_logic: Task records whose assignment_group sys_id has no corresponding group record
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence across all task tables
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — the record exists or it does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Task count by table, the missing group sys_ids, the tasks' ages and states, and the deletion event if retained.
rules.false_positive_guard: None. This is always a defect.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — reassignment is an operational decision

rules.rule: Approver reference pointing to a deleted or inactive record
rules.what_it_means: An approver reference points to a deleted or inactive record.
rules.why_it_matters: The approval is generated against a record that cannot approve. The request hangs with no error, which is the defining failure mode of this dimension.
rules.source_tables_fields: Approval records and configuration, referenced user and group existence and state
rules.detection_logic: Approval references resolving to non-existent or inactive records
rules.threshold_parameter: Report deleted and inactive separately
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on existence and state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Approval records, the broken references, the requests blocked, and their ages.
rules.false_positive_guard: Inactive with a configured delegate.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Catalog item referencing a retired workflow or missing variable set
rules.what_it_means: A catalog item references a retired workflow or a missing variable set.
rules.why_it_matters: Requests submitted against it fail at fulfilment or produce an incomplete record. The failure occurs after the user has submitted, so it looks like a system fault.
rules.source_tables_fields: sc_cat_item workflow and variable set references, target existence and state
rules.detection_logic: Catalog items referencing workflows or variable sets that are retired, inactive or absent
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence on active items
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on reference existence and state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Item, the broken reference, order volume, the open requests affected, and their states.
rules.false_positive_guard: Item inactive and retained for history.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2

rules.rule: Reference field pointing to a deleted record
rules.what_it_means: A reference field points to a record that has been deleted.
rules.why_it_matters: The generic case. Any consumer reading the reference gets nothing, and depending on the consumer it either errors or silently treats the field as empty.
rules.source_tables_fields: Reference field values across configured tables, target record existence
rules.detection_logic: Reference values whose target sys_id has no corresponding record
rules.threshold_parameter: Scope to operationally significant reference fields; the full scan is expensive
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — the record exists or it does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Broken reference count by table and field, sample records, and the deletion events if retained.
rules.false_positive_guard: References to records in tables outside the scan scope.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where the correct target is unambiguous, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: The generic form of DQ-125 to DQ-127

rules.rule: Asset-to-CI link broken in one direction
rules.what_it_means: The asset-to-CI link is broken in one direction — the asset references the CI but not the reverse, or vice versa.
rules.why_it_matters: Traversal works one way and fails the other. Which system you start from determines whether you find the counterpart.
rules.source_tables_fields: alm_asset ci field, cmdb_ci asset field, bidirectional comparison
rules.detection_logic: Asset-CI pairs where the reference exists in one direction only
rules.threshold_parameter: Report each direction separately
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the bidirectional comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: The pairs, which direction is populated, last update on each, and the count by asset class.
rules.false_positive_guard: Classes where a one-directional link is the intended model.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — complete the reverse reference, reversible

rules.rule: Notification recipient resolving to nothing
rules.what_it_means: A notification recipient configuration resolves to nothing — no user, no group member, no valid address.
rules.why_it_matters: The notification fires and reaches nobody, and the notification log records it as sent. There is no failure signal anywhere.
rules.source_tables_fields: Notification rule recipient configuration, resolution at evaluation time
rules.detection_logic: Notification rules whose recipient configuration resolves to an empty recipient set
rules.threshold_parameter: Resolution evaluated live
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on resolution.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, recipient configuration, resolution result, firing volume, and the records that triggered it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Conditional notifications that legitimately resolve empty in some cases.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Knowledge article referenced in resolutions but retired or unpublished
rules.what_it_means: Knowledge articles referenced in incident resolutions are retired or unpublished.
rules.why_it_matters: Agents are citing guidance that has been withdrawn. Either the retirement was wrong or the resolutions are following stale material.
rules.source_tables_fields: Incident-to-article references, kb_knowledge state
rules.detection_logic: Article references from resolutions where the article is retired or unpublished
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on article state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Article, state and retirement date, the resolutions citing it since, and any replacement article.
rules.false_positive_guard: Article retired after the resolutions were written.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3
rules.cross_domain_link: Duplicates ITSM-139 from the data quality side

rules.rule: Report or dashboard referencing a deleted field
rules.what_it_means: A report or dashboard references a field that has been deleted.
rules.why_it_matters: The report errors or silently omits a column. Dashboards degrade quietly, and the people relying on them do not know what is missing.
rules.source_tables_fields: Report and dashboard definitions, referenced field existence in sys_dictionary
rules.detection_logic: Report and dashboard field references with no corresponding dictionary entry
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence on active reports
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on dictionary existence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Report or dashboard, the missing field, its owner, schedule if scheduled, and distribution list.
rules.false_positive_guard: Field on a table the report no longer uses.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: PAN, Aadhaar or account-number patterns in free-text fields
rules.what_it_means: Free-text fields contain values matching PAN, Aadhaar or account-number patterns.
rules.why_it_matters: Personal identifiers entering ServiceNow through description and notes fields, unclassified and usually with broad read access. Under DPDP this is processing without classification, and the incident process is the most common entry route.
rules.source_tables_fields: Free-text fields across task, user and catalog tables; identifier regex with checksum validation where the format supports it
rules.detection_logic: Field values matching identifier patterns, counted by field, table and pattern type
rules.threshold_parameter: Pattern set per identifier. PAN and Aadhaar support checksum validation; apply it and report validated matches separately.
rules.confidence_basis: Checksum-validated match 95%. Pattern-only match 75%. Always report the two separately and never merge them.
rules.evidence_to_show: COUNT AND LOCATION ONLY — never the matched values, never in the finding, never in the report. Report table, field, pattern type, count, and the ACL state on those fields.
rules.false_positive_guard: Numeric strings coincidentally matching the pattern. Checksum validation removes most; report unvalidated matches as indicative only.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — redaction is a data protection decision requiring legal input, never a bulk edit
rules.cross_domain_link: Feeds DPDP Compliance Manager and the Regulatory Evidence Pack

rules.rule: Personal data in fields with no ACL protection
rules.what_it_means: Personal data sits in fields with no ACL protection.
rules.why_it_matters: Anyone with table read access can read it. The classification may be correct and the access control is absent, which is the gap that turns a data holding into a breach.
rules.source_tables_fields: Fields identified as holding personal data, sys_security_acl coverage for those fields
rules.detection_logic: Personal-data fields with no field-level ACL, or covered only by a permissive table-level ACL
rules.threshold_parameter: Personal data field set from classification where it exists, otherwise from DQ-133 detection
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on ACL coverage. Field classification confidence depends on its source.
rules.evidence_to_show: Field, table, the ACL coverage, the roles that can read it, and the record count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Protection applied at the table level and genuinely adequate.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — ACL as update set

rules.rule: Personal data in attachments on records with broad read access
rules.what_it_means: Personal data appears in attachments on records with broad read access.
rules.why_it_matters: Attachments inherit the record's access. A document attached to an incident is readable by everyone who can read that incident, and attachment content is rarely reviewed.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_attachment on records with broad read ACLs, attachment metadata and content classification
rules.detection_logic: Attachments on records whose read ACL is broad, where content classification indicates personal data
rules.threshold_parameter: Content classification method must be stated; metadata-only detection is weaker than content scanning
rules.confidence_basis: Metadata-based detection 60%. Content-based detection 85%. State which was used.
rules.evidence_to_show: Attachment count by record type and ACL breadth, file types, and the read roles — never the content itself.
rules.false_positive_guard: Attachments correctly classified and access-controlled at the record level.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3

rules.rule: Personal data present beyond the defined retention period
rules.what_it_means: Personal data is present beyond the defined retention period.
rules.why_it_matters: Retention is a DPDP obligation, not a housekeeping preference. Data held past its period is processing without a lawful basis.
rules.source_tables_fields: Records holding personal data, creation and closure dates, retention policy periods
rules.detection_logic: Personal-data-holding records older than the applicable retention period with no archival or deletion
rules.threshold_parameter: Retention periods from the customer's policy; report the absence of a policy as DQ-139
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on date arithmetic where a policy period exists.
rules.evidence_to_show: Record count by table and age band, the applicable retention period, and the archival or deletion configuration state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legal hold or regulatory retention requirement overriding the standard period.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — deletion requires legal confirmation

rules.rule: Custom field storing identifier-class data with no classification
rules.what_it_means: A custom field stores identifier-class data with no data classification applied.
rules.why_it_matters: Somebody built a field to hold an identifier and nobody classified it. It sits outside every protection and retention mechanism that classification would have triggered.
rules.source_tables_fields: Custom field definitions, content pattern analysis, data classification metadata
rules.detection_logic: Custom fields whose content matches identifier patterns, with no classification metadata
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires where a classification framework exists on the instance
rules.confidence_basis: Pattern-based content detection at 80%. Report with samples of the field, never the values.
rules.evidence_to_show: Field, table, population count, the pattern type detected, the ACL state, and the classification framework state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Field correctly classified through an external register.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — classification and ACL as update set

rules.rule: Personal data replicated into non-production instances
rules.what_it_means: Personal data has been replicated into non-production instances.
rules.why_it_matters: Sub-production instances typically have weaker access control, wider developer access and no retention enforcement. Cloning production into them is the most common way personal data escapes its controls.
rules.source_tables_fields: Non-production instance data, clone configuration and data scrub rules, personal data field population
rules.detection_logic: Personal-data fields populated in non-production instances, joined to the clone scrub configuration
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires access to the non-production instance, or evidence from the clone configuration
rules.confidence_basis: 100% where the non-production instance can be assessed. Clone-configuration-only assessment at 80%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Instance, the personal data fields populated, record counts, the clone scrub configuration, and the access roles on that instance.
rules.false_positive_guard: Non-production data synthetically generated rather than cloned.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — clone scrub rule configuration

rules.rule: No data classification applied to tables holding personal data
rules.what_it_means: No data classification is applied to tables holding personal data.
rules.why_it_matters: Without classification there is no mechanism to apply protection, retention or subject-access handling consistently. Every other finding in this dimension is a consequence of this one, which is why it is Systemic.
rules.source_tables_fields: Data classification configuration, tables identified as holding personal data
rules.detection_logic: Tables holding personal data with no classification metadata applied
rules.threshold_parameter: Personal data identification from DQ-133 detection and from field semantics
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on classification absence. Table identification confidence from the detection method.
rules.evidence_to_show: Table list with personal data field counts, record volumes, classification state, and the retention and ACL configuration each lacks.
rules.false_positive_guard: Classification maintained in an external register with documented linkage.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of DQ-134, DQ-136, DQ-137, DQ-138
